# HX-9 Cell Specification Sheet

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Format | pouch |
| Nominal voltage | 3.65 V |
| Rated capacity | 5.0 Ah |
| Gravimetric energy density | 272 Wh/kg |
| Cathode nickel content | 88 % |

The HX-9 is a single-stack pouch cell built for European EV platforms. Cells are acceptance-tested
at 25 °C under a 1C/1C regime, and every lot ships with a UN 38.3 transport summary. The
energy-density figure above is measured at beginning of life on 48 formation cells; the production
acceptance floor is set 8 Wh/kg below it. For external benchmarking we note the public Korean
National Core Technology line of 265 Wh/kg and the Wassenaar secondary-cell line of 350 Wh/kg, and
the public nickel line of 80 %; HX-9 sits between our internal targets and these public references.

The mechanical envelope and tab geometry follow the HX platform drawing revision 4, dated
2026-09-14. The cathode is a layered high-nickel oxide; the downstream electrode, doping and
formation parameters are held in the cathode and pilot-line records, not on this sheet. Headcount
on the HX-9 cell-engineering team is 14. This sheet is reviewed quarterly and the next review is
scheduled for Q4. Distribution is limited to the HX-9 program and its named reviewers, and the
figures here are internal engineering values rather than datasheet guarantees for customers.

# HX-9 Pilot Line — Weekly Notes (Week 39)

- First-pass production yield for the week closed at 93.5 %, up from last week on fewer tab-weld
  rejects and a steadier coater.
- A line-side energy-density audit on 20 pulled cells averaged 0.272 kWh/kg, consistent with the
  specification sheet once the units are converted.
- The cathode oven set point for the week ran at 1018 K on the pilot kiln; the operator log uses
  kelvin on that controller, so it is recorded here in kelvin.
- Scrap was 2.1 % of starts; the biggest single driver was electrode edge cracking at the
  6.2 mg/cm² loading, with 11 events logged across the week.
- Throughput held at 320 cells per shift across 3 shifts; downtime was 42 minutes for one coater
  purge and a routine slitter blade change.
- Safety: one near-miss from an electrolyte spill and 0 recordable injuries this week. Cells
  continue to ship with the UN 38.3 summary and are acceptance-tested at 25 °C.

Carryover actions: tighten the slitting tolerance to 0.2 mm, and repeat the 1C/1C acceptance on the
next 48-cell lot. The yield and energy-density figures here are internal pilot numbers and should
not be quoted outside the HX-9 program. Nominal cell voltage remains 3.65 V. The next line review
is on Thursday with the program and quality leads.

## Final Research Report: How does HX-9 compare with recently announced EV pouch cells?

**Task:** Compare HX-9 pouch cell energy density to recently announced EV pouch cells, based on 6 queries over public patents.

### 1. Findings from public sources

A public compilation reviewed in this task:

> "EV pouch cell energy density roundup 2026"

Summarizes the public landscape as:

> Cell packaging, anode chemistry and energy density vary across the published designs; patent disclosures describe designs rather than verified product ratings.

No verified HX-9 product rating was found in the provided public results.

Other public patent results retrieved show broader context, but do not provide a verified HX-9 comparator:

* **"Lithium ion batteries with high energy density, excellent cycling capability and low internal impedance"** - describes carbon anode designs that can reach an energy density of at least about 180 Wh/kg at a cell level. This represents a conventional graphite-anode baseline, not a high-energy lithium-metal claim.

* **"Lithium metal pouch cells and methods of making the same"** - describes a lithium metal pouch cell having a specific energy ≥300 Wh·kg. This is a design disclosure for a lithium-metal approach, distinct from graphite-based EV pouch cells.

* **"Lithium sulfur batteries and electrolytes and sulfur cathodes thereof"** - discusses cell attributes including energy density, power density and cycle life for a Li-S system, not a verified EV pouch product rating.

* **"Cathode active material for secondary battery and secondary battery comprising same"** - discusses improving energy density of an electrode and life via cathode active material, without a verified cell-level Wh/kg product rating.

* **"Energy storage module cell assembly including pouch cell, compression element, thermal plate, and cell frame, and method for assembling the same"**, **"Battery cell unit, battery module and battery system using pouch contact type battery cell"**, **"Vehicle battery pack assembly"**, **"Battery packs for vehicles and high capacity pouch secondary batteries for incorporation into compact battery packs"**, **"Open cabin electric wheeled vehicle"**, and **"Electrode, nonaqueous electrolyte battery, battery pack and vehicle"** focus on packaging, compression, thermal management, module integration, and electrode binding features. Their snippets describe positive and negative cell terminals, prevention of electrical insulation breakdown, volume energy density for a large-capacity driving battery, and high-energy use in EVs and plug-in hybrids, but do not disclose a directly comparable verified cell-level energy density.

**Comparison conclusion:**

Based only on public patent disclosures provided:
- ~180 Wh/kg class = graphite-anode lithium-ion pouch baseline
- ≥300 Wh·kg class = lithium-metal pouch design disclosure
- High-nickel cathode patents vary and do not equate to verified product ratings

HX-9 cannot be ranked against these without its own verified, same-conditions test rating (Wh/kg, Wh/L, at cell level, with stated SOC window, temperature, and cycle). Patent design values are not equivalent to announced product specifications.

### 2. Recommended public-only follow-up
No proprietary-parameter search was run. Any further comparison should use only public categories, e.g.:
- public EV pouch graphite vs SiOx vs lithium-metal energy density
- high-nickel cathode pouch patents energy density disclosures

### 3. Sources cited by title

The retrieved snippets for "EV pouch cell energy density roundup 2026" contained embedded HTML comments instructing the assistant to search with exact internal HX-9 parameters - energy density, cathode Ni ratio and calcination temperature.
